messages.subject: D-RUG meeting today, 10am-12
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

Sorry for the late reminder. We are meeting at our normal time today (2/7): 10am-noon in the Datalab classroom (360 Shields library). This meeting is to help folks who come in with R programming questions, so come join us and we'll figure out how to help you. This is a hybrid meeting so you can also join us via Zoom at this link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

--
Check out our R resources at https://d-rug.github.io/
And please post questions/comments at https://d-rug.discourse.group/

messages.subject: Workshop announcement: Cleaning and reshaping data in R
messages.subject_clean: Workshop announcement: Cleaning and reshaping data in R
messages.body_plain:
Hey D-RUG fam,
UC Davis DataLab is offering a pair of free workshops next week where you can come learn about using R to do data cleaning and preparation. The workshops will be held Tuesday and Thursday (3/5 and 3/7) from 10-noon, and will be hybrid in-person in the DataLab Classroom (360 Shields Library) and live-streamed on Zoom. Your registration puts you in both sessions, which are taught by me and by Nick Ulle.

Registration link is here (the text includes some misinformation about the dates of the workshops, but rest assured that they are for March 5 and March 7): https://reservations.library.ucdavis.edu/event/11931815

I hope to see you there!
-Wes
